settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: The reviewed code never calls any Digester/SAXFactory feature setter; whether XXE actually fires therefore depends on library/runtime defaults not visible in the read source.
analysis-core 1.94 and commons-digester versions are declared in pom.xml but their parser-factory defaults were not inspected (dependency sources unavailable in the read spans).
The parser is used to read build-generated report files; Jenkins may consider the workspace untrusted, but the concrete reachability of an attacker-controlled file was not demonstrated.
No entity resolver or explicit external-entity enablement exists either, so there is no positive evidence the code intentionally allows entities.
candidates.description: CcmParser.parseCCMXmlFile(InputStream) builds a new org.apache.commons.digester.Digester and configures only setValidating(false) and setClassLoader(...), then registers object/property rules and calls digester.parse(ccmXmlFile). No call disables DOCTYPE declarations, external general/parameter entities, or enables secure processing on the underlying SAX parser factory. The InputStream originates from the build workspace: CcmPublisher.perform passes a FilesParser over the workspace to a new CcmParser(getDefaultEncoding()) (lines 94-98), and the Maven path CcmReporter.perform does the same over getTargetPath(pom) (lines 131-135). Thus a malicious ccm XML file committed to the repository, produced by a prior build step, or dropped in the workspace and matching the configured Ant pattern (**/*.cs by default) is parsed in the Jenkins controller JVM. With external entity resolution enabled by the parser's runtime defaults, a crafted DOCTYPE with SYSTEM entities could read local files or make outbound requests from the controller. The repository itself contains XXE-shaped fixtures (testXxe-xxe.xml with <!ENTITY % sp SYSTEM "$OOB_LINK$"> and %sp;/%param1; expansion; testXxe-oob.xml with an out-of-band entity definition), which is consistent with external-entity parsing being relevant to this parser. The root cause is missing parser hardening in the Digester setup rather than a logic error; effectiveness depends on the underlying SAX parser factory defaults not being secure by default, which could not be verified from the read sources. Reported as a candidate, not a confirmed exploitable XXE.
missing_evidence: The actual Apache Commons Digester / SAX parser factory defaults in the resolved dependency versions (features such as disallow-doctype-decl, external-general-entities, external-parameter-entities, XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING).
Whether any hosting/analysis-core wrapper sets parser features before CcmParser.parse is invoked (FilesParser / AbstractAnnotationParser implementation not read).
A runtime test (or existing test referencing testXxe-*.xml) that would confirm an external entity is actually fetched or a local file is read.
Whether Jenkins' permission model restricts who can influence the workspace file matching the configured pattern in the target deployment.
preconditions: A CCM plugin publisher/reporter is configured for the job with a file pattern that matches an attacker-influenceable file (default pattern **/*.cs).
An attacker can place/commit a crafted ccm XML file in the build workspace (e.g., via SCM commit or a build step) matching the configured pattern.
The underlying SAX parser factory used by the Digester instance resolves external DTD/entities (not explicitly disabled in this code).
A build runs and the publisher's perform() executes on the controller.
candidates.title: XML parser in CcmParser is created with Apache Commons Digester without disabling DTD/external entities (XXE hardening absent)
